Article Title: Midterm blues: Why a 'lame' duck Donald Trump may push for a quick India-US trade deal
Article Text:
Both Democrats and Republicans have increasingly backed economic nationalism. (Image for representative purpose only)

What this means for India-US trade deal

What does Democrats’ win in US midterm elections mean for India-US trade deal prospects? Will Donald Trump be forced to change his strategy?The unfavourable midterm election outcome is unlikely to prompt President Donald Trump to change course on trade, according to an analysis by Global Trade Research Initiative (GTRI).But, it’s important to note that both Democrats and Republicans have increasingly backed economic nationalism, domestic manufacturing and the strengthening of supply chains.Democratic lawmakers, too, favour protective tariffs to safeguard unionised workers and local industries.“The adverse midterm results won’t change President Donald Trump’s trade direction because both Democrats and Republicans now favor economic nationalism, domestic manufacturing, and strong supply chains,” says Ajay Srivastava, founder of GTRI.Unable to rely on Congress for every measure, Trump is expected to continue exercising powers already available to the administration. These include Sections 232 and 301, along with executive orders, Treasury sanctions and rules issued by the Office of the United States Trade Representative (USTR), to exert unilateral pressure on trading partners.According to GTRI, with foreign policy leverage failing against Russia, China, and Iran, Trump needs a quick win.“Expect heightened pressure on India for a trade deal to prove American clout,” he says.For several months, leaders on both sides have indicated that a trade agreement is close to being finalised. However, the lack of clarity over the US offer appears to have held up its completion, the think tank says.Trump is now likely to use his executive authority to push India towards an early agreement that opens up the Indian market to American agricultural and industrial products, while securing other significant concessions for US businesses.The agreement under negotiation between India and the US is fundamentally different from the other free trade agreements (FTAs) India has entered into. Under conventional trade agreements, both participating countries reduce or eliminate their regular import duties, which are governed by World Trade Organization (WTO) rules and referred to as Most Favoured Nation (MFN) tariffs.The proposed US–India framework, however, follows a different approach. Washington would continue to levy its regular MFN duties, while India would be required to eliminate or lower such tariffs on most industrial products and a wide range of agricultural goods.The February 6 US–India Joint Statement sets out further commitments for India. These include aligning its security and economic policies with Washington, purchasing $500 billion worth of American goods over five years, and relaxing domestic regulatory oversight of imports from the US.“The US may be relying on the threat of additional tariffs to secure India's compliance. These include potential measures linked to India's purchases of Russian oil under the Graham Act and Section 301,” Srivastava notes.Also, signing the agreement would not necessarily protect India from further tariff action. The US could still impose additional duties of 15% to 18% over and above its standard MFN rates. In effect, the proposed arrangement would amount to economic coercion.“India should not mistake relief from threatened tariffs for a balanced trade agreement. Opening its markets, committing to large purchases and limiting its policy choices would carry lasting costs, while any U.S. tariff relief could prove temporary. New Delhi should insist on clear, enforceable reciprocal concessions, consistency with WTO rules and full freedom to protect its energy security and development priorities. The pressure to announce a deal must not outweigh the need to secure one that serves India’s long-term interests,” Srivastava says.
Article Summary: Both Democrats and Republicans have increasingly backed economic nationalism. The US could still impose additional duties of 15% to 18% over and above its standard MFN rates. In effect, the proposed arrangement would amount to economic coercion. India should not mistake relief from threatened tariffs for a balanced trade agreement.

Article Title: Elon Musk's nearly $500 million US midterm gamble backfires: Tesla, SpaceX stocks take a hit
Article Text:
Musk's political gamble falls flat, Tesla, SpaceX stocks take a hit

Why Musk's businesses could feel the political heat

Where Musk's $474 million election money went

Musk was not the only tech billionaire backing Trump

Elon Musk poured nearly half a billion dollars into the US midterm elections, but lost the gamble. As Democrats seized control of both chambers of Congress and Gina Hinojosa defeated Greg Abbott in the Texas governor's race, shares of Musk-owned companies came under pressure.Shares of Musk-owned companies came under pressure, with SpaceX falling 3.8% in premarket trading and Tesla slipping 3.6%. Both stocks underperformed the broader market.The decline came even as US equities rallied following the midterm elections. The S&P 500 jumped 1.6%, gaining 119.7 points to close at 7,688.62. The Nasdaq Composite added 364.50 points, or 1.4%, to 25,736.51, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average surged 1,569.40 points, or 3%, to 53,356.12. The Dow rose more than 1,500 points during the session.US stocks have historically tended to gain following midterm elections, regardless of which party wins. However, Musk's businesses moved in the opposite direction as the election results dealt a blow to the Republicans and US President Donald Trump, a close ally whom the billionaire helped elect.The setback is particularly significant given Musk's business interests in Texas, which houses his electric vehicle maker Tesla, his rocket-to-AI company SpaceX and a planned chipmaking venture between the two.His election spending was aimed at helping Republican candidates retain their positions and keeping Texas red.An analysis by The New York Times suggests that Musk contributed $474 million to Republican candidates during the 2026 midterms, including almost $224 million in Texas alone, making him the biggest donor of the election by a considerable margin.The Democratic victory could have significant implications for Musk's companies, particularly SpaceX's plans to build data centres. Slower approvals for these facilities could become a major hurdle as the company looks to tap the $28.5 trillion addressable market it presented to investors ahead of its IPO.With Democrats now controlling both chambers of Congress, analysts and experts expect greater scrutiny of data-centre projects and possible pushes for construction moratoriums amid growing local opposition over electricity costs.Musk has already faced scrutiny from Democratic lawmakers over restrictions on satellite communications used by Ukraine, mass federal job cuts at DOGE, and government contracts and subsidies flowing to his companies. The stronger Democratic presence in Congress could bring these issues back into focus.The latest market reaction also comes after a strong recovery in Tesla shares. The stock has rallied 34% since its late-July low, supported by investor optimism surrounding its artificial intelligence products and the potential combination with SpaceX.SpaceX, meanwhile, entered the ranks of the world's most valuable companies after going public earlier this year. The company generates billions of dollars through US government contracts, but its shares have largely remained flat since its June IPO, holding on to a massive $1.9 trillion market valuation.Musk's companies have previously shown sensitivity to election outcomes. Following Trump's re-election in 2024, Tesla shares surged more than 90% in little over a month. However, those gains later unwound as Musk's relationship with Trump soured and investors grew tired of his involvement in the Department of Government Efficiency.A significant portion of Musk's election spending flowed through political action committees supporting Republican candidates across the country.His America PAC, the super PAC he owns, received $216 million and was active in more than 40 House and Senate races. According to Newsweek, Musk contributed another $77 million to the group in the first half of October alone.The Senate Leadership Fund, the main super PAC backing Senate Republicans, received $168 million. Of this amount, $158 million was passed on to Texas PAC, the biggest supporter of Republican Ken Paxton.Musk also contributed $30 million to the Congressional Leadership Fund to help protect the Republican majority in the House. His trust gave another $10 million to Lone Star Liberty PAC, the main outside group supporting Paxton.His involvement in Republican fundraising is not new. In 2024, Musk spent nearly $300 million backing Trump and other Republican candidates.Musk's political contributions were the largest among four technology billionaires who backed Trump. Oracle co-founder Larry Ellison, Michael Dell and Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff also supported the president through financial contributions, charitable commitments and White House projects.Ellison contributed around $45 million to a nonprofit supporting Trump's 2024 campaign, according to The Wall Street Journal. The donation remained undisclosed until June 2026. He later praised Trump at the White House event announcing the Stargate AI project, telling him, "We certainly couldn’t do this without you". Trump described Ellison as the "CEO of everything".Michael Dell and his wife Susan pledged $6.25 billion to fund "Trump Accounts". The money will go to the US Treasury and be deposited in $250 amounts into accounts for 25 million children aged 10 or younger. The programme targets children in zip codes where the median income is $150,000 or less. Trump later urged Americans to buy Dell computers, following which the company's stock rose more than 7%.Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff also backed Trump, marking a shift from his earlier political contributions, a major share of which went to Democrats. He committed $1 million towards Trump's White House ballroom, while Salesforce separately made two commitments of $1 million each. Benioff later faced criticism for supporting the deployment of National Guard troops in San Francisco, a proposal opposed by local city leaders. He subsequently withdrew his remarks and apologised for calling in the Guard.
Article Summary: Elon Musk poured nearly half a billion dollars into the US midterm elections. As Democrats seized control of both chambers of Congress, shares of Musk-owned companies came under pressure. SpaceX fell 3.8% in premarket trading and Tesla slipped 3.6%. Both stocks underperformed the broader market.

Article Title: Crude crashes below $100: Brent, WTI hit over two-month lows as Trump loses US midterm elections
Article Text:
Crude prices fall below $100 per barrel

Trump faces pressure as war weighs on Republicans

Qatar steps up mediation as Iran deal remains distant

Oil prices continued to ease on Thursday, with Brent crude and US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) tumbling below the $100-per-barrel threshold.Brent slipped below the $95-per-barrel mark, while WTI fell below $90, as markets continued to react to the political fallout of the US midterm elections and the possibility of an end to the war with Iran.Brent crude futures fell 50 cents, or 0.53%, to $94.12 a barrel, while WTI crude declined 61 cents, or 0.69%, to $87.51.The latest movement follows Wednesday's sharp sell-off, when both benchmarks lost more than 8% and settled at their lowest levels in over two months. Brent ended the session at $94.62 a barrel, shedding $8.98 or 8.7%, while WTI settled at $88.12, down $7.97 or 8.3%. Both contracts recorded their lowest closing levels since August 31.The market reaction came after Republicans lost control of Congress in the midterm elections, raising expectations that US President Donald Trump could face greater pressure to bring the US-Israeli war with Iran to an end.The election outcome has also complicated Washington's options in the conflict. With Democrats taking control of the House of Representatives and the Senate, Trump could find it harder to pursue further military action.Two sources close to Gulf government circles told Reuters that the weakened political position gave him greater reason to pursue a negotiated settlement, making a full-scale assault on Iran less likely.However, the possibility of a deal does not necessarily rule out further escalation. Gulf analysts said an agreement that allows Iran to claim a clear victory while leaving Trump appearing defeated could encourage recklessness rather than restraint.Trump told the Financial Times earlier this week that the US had no immediate plans to strike Iran. A day later, he acknowledged that the conflict had contributed to his party's sweeping defeat in the midterm elections.Vice president JD Vance also questioned the decision to enter the war on Wednesday, distancing himself from it and blaming the conflict entirely for the Republicans' electoral setback.Tehran, however, has indicated that a change in political control in Washington would not alter its position towards the US. Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei said in a written statement that American hostility would continue regardless of which party was in power.There were also fresh developments in the region, with Yemen's Houthis claiming to have targeted King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh.Diplomatic efforts to prevent another escalation have gathered pace, with Qatar stepping up mediation following the US elections. But the prospect of an immediate breakthrough remains uncertain.Meanwhile, regional energy flows continue to be disrupted. The United Arab Emirates is also looking at ways to reduce its reliance on the Strait of Hormuz, considering a third oil pipeline.Separately, US oil stockpiles recorded a decline last week. The Energy Information Administration said crude inventories dropped by 865,000 barrels to 409.8 million barrels in the week ended October 30. This was sharply different from expectations in a Reuters poll, where analysts had forecast an increase of 877,000 barrels.
Article Summary: Brent slipped below the $95-per-barrel mark, while WTI fell below $90. Market reaction came after Republicans lost control of Congress in the midterm elections, raising expectations that Donald Trump could face greater pressure to bring the US-Israeli war with Iran to an end.

Article Title: Trump tariff taxes Republicans: What US midterm results mean for Indian H-1B visa holders, Russian oil & trade deal
Article Text:
American voters have handed control of the US Congress to the opposition Democratic Party.

The results are expected to have implications extending beyond the US - so what does this mean for India? Let’s take a look:

What it means for H-1B visa holders and green card aspirants

India’s purchase of Russian oil

India-US trade deal & tariffs

US President Donald Trump has suffered a major blow in midterm elections with Republicans losing control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate.In a significant rebuke to Trump, American voters on Tuesday handed control of the US Congress to the opposition Democratic Party and shifted several key gubernatorial positions in closely watched elections.Trump's Republican Party suffered major defeats in its strongholds, including Texas, Georgia and Iowa, losing the governors' offices to Democratic candidates.Trump’s policies are being blamed by many as the reason for the loss - with tariffs and inflation in focus.US President Donald Trump has tightened access to H-1B visas through a $100,000 fee and a wage-weighted selection system, making it harder for Indian professionals to secure US jobs. His administration has also suspended eight technology companies from the PERM green card programme, disrupting some workers’ routes to permanent residency and green cards. So will the midterm results change that attitude?No. Not much is expected to change on this front, despite Trump’s loss. This is because both Democrats and Republicans prioritise domestic employment.According to Ajay Srivastava, founder of Global Trade Research Initiative (GTRI), tighter immigration policies find bipartisan support.“Be it the Biden administration or the Trump one, policies are increasingly becoming restrictive and that approach is unlikely to change,” Srivastava tells TOI.Also Read | ‘Death by restriction’: As Trump sours H-1B visa dream, which Indian IT professionals face the biggest hit? According to Rajiv Dabhadkar, Founder, National Organization For Software and Technology Professionals, the H-1B debate has moved beyond party politics to a fundamental US policy challenge: protecting American jobs while retaining access to global talent.“Regardless of the outcome of the midterm elections, the US is looking to address long-standing flaws in the immigration system, including wage protections, worker displacement and how employers use foreign professionals,” he tells TOI.What fundamentally needs to be understood is that H-1B reform is now a bipartisan American policy imperative, not merely a political reaction to one administration, he adds.Earlier this year, the Donald Trump administration managed to get support for the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026. The Act allows the US President to impose tariffs of up to 100% on countries importing oil from Russia and Iran in a big way.India and China lead the lot of Russian oil buyers. Recently, Trump announced a waiver on those tariffs for India. But, it’s important to note that the waiver was only for a period of 60 days.Also Read | Does Trump’s 60-day tariff waiver really give relief to India? What it means for US trade deal & oil prices The Republicans losing control of the Congress is unlikely to change the Trump administration’s stance on buyers of Russian crude oil. This is because the bill enjoyed bipartisan support - both Democrats and Republicans appear keen to penalise buyers of Russian oil.However, what may work in India’s favour for now is America’s own diesel deal with Russia and the need by the Trump administration and even the Democrats to keep oil prices in check. Sanctioning Russian oil or penalising buyers of Moscow’s crude will not help that cause.So, for now India continues to enjoy relief from the prospect of 100% tariffs for its crude oil procurement from Russia, but this may work as a pressure tactic by the US to finalise a trade deal.For India, which is still negotiating a trade agreement with the United States, the outcome of the midterm elections could strengthen the case for taking a cautious, wait-and-watch approach.Earlier this month, Commerce minister Piyush Goyal said the first phase of the India-US trade agreement was in the final stages of drafting. However, he stressed that New Delhi would move ahead only if the terms gave Indian exporters an edge over their competitors.India and the US have already finalised a framework for the first phase of the Bilateral Trade Agreement. However, changes in the US tariff environment have led to further negotiations. India is seeking tariff rates on its exports that are more favourable than those faced by competing countries.In the meantime, experts believe the midterm setback could prompt Trump to pursue an early trade agreement with India. They said that with Washington struggling to exercise foreign policy leverage over Russia, China and Iran, Trump may look for quick success on the trade front.However, the economic think tank GTRI said the unfavourable midterm outcome was unlikely to fundamentally alter Trump's trade policy. Both Republicans and Democrats, it noted, support economic nationalism, domestic manufacturing and robust supply chains."With foreign policy leverage failing against Russia, China, and Iran, Trump needs a quick win. Expect heightened pressure on India for a trade deal to prove American clout and the midterm losses may push Trump to seek a quick India trade deal," said Ajay Srivastava.Federation of Indian Export Organisations (FIEO) president SC Ralhan said the US continues to be an important destination for Indian goods and services."What will matter to Indian exporters in the months ahead is how US policy on tariffs and market access takes shape. MSMEs in particular need predictable trading conditions to price orders confidently and plan shipments months in advance," he told PTI.
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump has suffered a major blow in midterm elections. Republicans lost control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate. The results are expected to have implications extending beyond the US. So what does this mean for India? Let’s take a look.

Article Title: Why new LNG projects may not prevent a global gas crunch this winter
Article Text:
Representative image

New LNG projects unlikely to offset Persian Gulf losses

IEA outlines two scenarios for winter gas supplies

Global natural gas supplies could tighten further during the 2026–27 winter heating season as disruptions to shipments through the Strait of Hormuz continue to affect the global liquefied natural gas (LNG) market, the International Energy Agency (IEA) has warned.In its report, the IEA described the disruption as an unprecedented supply shock, noting that LNG loadings from Qatar and the United Arab Emirates declined by 60 billion cubic metres (bcm) year-on-year between March and October 2026.This contributed to a 5 per cent, or 20 bcm, fall in global LNG output, as additional supplies from new projects only partly offset reduced deliveries from the Persian Gulf, according to news agency ANI.With transit through the Strait of Hormuz remaining severely restricted in late October, the agency warned that the disruption could continue to weigh on global gas supplies during the winter months."The disruption of LNG flows through the Strait of Hormuz creates unprecedented uncertainty for the global LNG market ahead of the 2026/27 winter," the report said.It added that "the supply shock looks set to keep imposing tighter market conditions during the northern hemisphere winter, even as supply from new liquefaction plants around the globe continues to grow."Depending on how quickly LNG shipments through the Strait of Hormuz recover, global LNG supply could decline by 10–25 bcm year-on-year between November and March, the IEA said.The scope for increasing pipeline gas supplies remains limited, as long-distance pipelines generally operate close to their designed capacity. This restricts their ability to compensate for shortages in LNG deliveries.North American exporters are expected to drive LNG supply growth during the winter, supported by expanding projects in the United States, Canada and Mexico. Additional volumes are also expected from new facilities in West Africa and Australia.The IEA projects that new LNG projects will add around 18 bcm of supply during the winter, while existing facilities could contribute another 3 bcm. This would take total incremental supply from outside the Persian Gulf to slightly over 20 bcm.However, the additional volumes are not expected to make up for the shortfall from Qatar and the UAE."In total, new and legacy projects outside the Persian Gulf could contribute slightly over 20 bcm of incremental supply y-o-y in the winter period. Despite the strong growth, this extra supply would remain insufficient to compensate for the lost volumes from Qatar and the United Arab Emirates," the report said.The agency outlined two possible scenarios depending on when the Strait of Hormuz resumes normal operations.If the waterway begins progressively reopening in January 2027, global LNG supply could decline by around 9 bcm, or 3 per cent, year-on-year during the winter period.However, if the Strait remains closed until the end of March 2027, the decline could be sharper, with global LNG supply falling by around 20 bcm, or 7 per cent, year-on-year.The IEA also cautioned that unplanned outages and delays in ramping up production at new LNG projects could create additional downside risks to global supplies, particularly while the disruption in the Middle East continues.
Article Summary: Disruption to shipments through the Strait of Hormuz continues to affect the global liquefied natural gas market. LNG loadings from Qatar and the United Arab Emirates declined by 60 billion cubic metres (bcm) year-on-year between March and October 2026.

Article Title: India's forex reserves dip by $2.69 billion: What's behind the decline?
Article Text:
Forex reserves shrink in October

NEW DELHI: India's foreign exchange reserves took a hit in the week ended October 30, falling by $2.691 billion to $717.056 billion, according to the latest data released by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on Friday.The decline was largely driven by a drop in two key components of the country's reserves, foreign currency assets and gold holdings, which together make up the bulk of the forex kitty.While foreign currency assets and gold reserves fell, India's reserve position with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) recorded a marginal increase.Special Drawing Rights (SDRs), meanwhile, also saw a decline during the week.Foreign currency assets, the biggest part of India's foreign exchange reserves, declined by $2.088 billion to $591.118 billion during the reporting week.Gold reserves also fell by $559 million, taking their value to $102.591 billion.The decline was not limited to these two components. India's SDR holdings, which are reserve assets allocated by the IMF, dropped by $47 million to $18.558 billion.However, the country's reserve position with the IMF increased by $3 million to $4.790 billion.The fall in reserves was also visible in their rupee value. India's total foreign exchange reserves stood at Rs 68.09 lakh crore as of October 30, marking a decline of Rs 24,777 crore from the previous week.Despite the latest weekly decline, India's foreign exchange reserves remain higher than their levels at the end of March 2026.Since the end of March, the country's reserves have increased by $25.949 billion. In rupee terms, the increase during this period stood at Rs 2.55 lakh crore.A year-on-year comparison shows that India's foreign exchange reserves have increased by $27.324 billion, or Rs 6.86 lakh crore.Foreign currency assets registered the biggest increase among the reserve components, rising by $26.527 billion over the year. Gold reserves also increased by $865 million.On the other hand, SDR holdings declined by $87 million during the same period. India's reserve position with the IMF recorded an increase of $18 million.While the latest data shows a weekly decline in the country's foreign exchange reserves, the overall reserve position remains higher than both its end-March 2026 level and its level a year ago.
Article Summary: India's foreign exchange reserves fell by $2.691 billion to $717.056 billion in the week ended October 30. The decline was largely driven by a drop in two key components of the country's reserves, foreign currency assets and gold holdings.

Article Title: Stuck at work on Diwali? Firms offer employees longer breaks, better gifts and extra earnings
Article Text:
AI generated image, used only for representational purpose

Gifts employees actually want

WFH for those traveling home

When the festive spirit has to reach the workplace

Diwali duty comes with extra earnings

Stuck at a desk while the rest of the world is busy celebrating may not be the ideal Diwali plan. However, companies are rolling out a range of festive perks to make sure their employees don't miss out on the celebrations.From longer weekends and work-from-home options to gifts of their choice and office festivities, employers are finding different ways to make the festival special for their workforce.And for those who have to work while others celebrate, there are extra payouts and special treats to sweeten the deal.For employees at quick-commerce firm Zepto, the festive break has come a day earlier than scheduled. The company advanced its holiday from Tuesday to Monday, giving its workforce an additional day off after Diwali."We want our people to enjoy the festive season with their families by giving them a longer weekend to celebrate," Sneha Arora, chief HR officer at the Bengaluru-headquartered firm told ET.At Hitachi India, employees had the opportunity to decide what they wanted as their festive gifts. The diversified manufacturer asked them to vote from a list of options, with air fryers and Amazon gift vouchers emerging as popular choices.Festive celebrations at the company also extended beyond gifts. Hitachi India hosted gatherings at hotels across the country, bringing together its Indian and Japanese employees, including senior leadership, said chief human resources officer Ashutosh Anshu.For employees planning to travel during Diwali, flexibility over where they work has also become part of the festive arrangements.Hitachi India's hybrid work policy allows employees to work from home for two days a week. This gives them room to manage festive travel and personal commitments, Anshu said.Aditya Mishra, chief executive at staffing and recruitment services firm CIEL HR Services, said greater flexibility in how employees celebrate has been a noticeable trend this festive season.Companies are extending work-from-home options wherever the nature of the job allows it, particularly for employees who want to travel to their hometowns but continue working."more work-from-home options are given wherever the nature of the role permits, to help employees who wish to travel to their hometowns and continue working", he said.Not everyone gets to switch off during Diwali. Employees working in housekeeping, security, office support, electrical and maintenance roles may still need to keep offices functioning during the celebrations.Proptech firm NoBroker.com is organising special festivities for these teams, along with a role-reversal exercise involving its HR department.Under the initiative, HR employees will take on the responsibilities usually handled by support staff for a few hours. This includes staffing office floors, managing security and ensuring that operations continue, allowing the employees in these roles to participate in the celebrations."For those few hours, our HR team steps into their shoes, staffing the floors, managing security and keeping the offices running, so that not a single person has to miss the festivities," said chief executive Amit Kumar Agarwal.For employees whose work involves being on the road, festive celebrations are also taking the form of additional financial incentives.Trev Mobility, an electric vehicles-focused cab-hailing service, has introduced a special incentive programme for its driver-partners working during Diwali, according to ET. The additional payouts will be over and above their regular earnings for working on designated festive days, said founder Naveen Gupta.The amount drivers can earn will depend on how many days they choose to work. Those available for just one or two days can also qualify for additional earnings, while driver-partners who complete all four designated days of duty, including Diwali, will be eligible for a significantly enhanced payout.Under the programme, those completing all four days will receive double payment, Gupta said."The incentive is structured around the number of days they choose to work, so even those available for one or two days can earn extra. Those who complete all four designated days of duty, including Diwali, are eligible for a significantly enhanced payout, with double payment under the programme," he added.
Article Summary: Employers are rolling out a range of festive perks to make sure their employees don't miss out on the celebrations. From longer weekends and work-from-home options to gifts of their choice and office festivities, employers are finding different ways to make the festival special for their workforce.

Kleros says Singapore court has ordered authorities to take action in $650Mn award

MUMBAI: Tata Power's legal battle with Kleros Capital Partners, a British Virgin Islands-incorporated resource and infrastructure investment firm, has taken a significant turn after a Singapore court authorised the seizure and sale of shares held by the Tata Group utility in two of its Singapore-based subsidiaries to recover dues arising from a long-running arbitration dispute.In an announcement on Thursday, Kleros said the Singapore International Commercial Court (SICC) has granted enforcement orders empowering the Sheriff of the Singapore courts to seize and sell Tata Power's shareholdings in Bhira Investments and Tata Power International.The move follows the SICC's decision in Aug to dismiss all challenges filed by Tata Power against arbitration awards issued in favour of Kleros.The enforcement action stems from a dispute over the Krutogorovo coal deposit in Russia's Kamchatka region. Kleros and Tata Power had entered into agreements in 2013 and 2014 to explore a joint development of the deposit. However, Kleros later alleged that Tata Power used confidential information obtained under those agreements to pursue the Krutogorovo coal deposit independently.The investment firm initiated arbitration proceedings in Singapore in Nov 2020.In Sept 2023, a three-member tribunal, constituted under the Singapore International Arbitration Centre (SIAC), unanimously ruled that Tata Power had breached contractual obligations by misusing confidential information, circumventing Kleros and concealing material facts while pursuing the coal project on its own.In July 2025, the tribunal awarded Kleros damages of $490 million. Including interest and costs, the total amount now claimed by Kleros exceeds $650 million. According to Kleros, interest continues to accrue at about $71,600 per day.While Tata Power has appealed the SICC's Aug ruling before the Singapore Court of Appeal and the matter remains pending, Kleros said the appeal does not automatically suspend enforcement proceedings and that the company "has not sought a stay of enforcement". As a result, the arbitration awards remain "final, binding and immediately enforceable" under Singapore law.Earlier, the SICC dismissed Tata Power's challenges to the July 2025 SIAC arbitral awards, including its objections to the appointment of two arbitrators who participated in the majority decision forming the basis of the final award. SICC held that there had been no breach of natural justice or the fair hearing rule in the tribunal's conduct.At Tata Power's annual general meeting in July this year, chairman N Chandrasekaran, responding to a shareholder query on the Kleros matter, said the arbitration case remained under appeal and declined to comment further.The two Singapore entities targeted by the enforcement order are as follows: Bhira Investments holds Tata Power's Indonesian coal mining interests, including a 30% stake in PT Kaltim Prima Coal, while Tata Power International serves as the utility's overseas investment holding vehicle.The latest enforcement order, however, raises the stakes in what has become one of the largest arbitration-related claims faced by an Indian corporate entity.
Article Summary: Kleros says Singapore court has ordered authorities to take action in $650Mn award. Tata Power's legal battle with Kleros Capital Partners has taken a significant turn. The enforcement action stems from a dispute over the Krutogorovo coal deposit in Russia's Kamchatka region.

Article Title: Rules tightened for classifying gold-backed farm loans as PSL
Article Text:
.

MUMBAI: RBI has proposed tighter rules for classifying gold-backed farm loans as priority sector lending (PSL), requiring banks to verify borrowers' actual agricultural credit needs against the district scale of finance for the crop. Banks would also have to document field inspections, crop hypothecation and evidence of agricultural activity by landless cultivators failing which loans will be classified as the more expensive gold loans.Under RBI's consolidated priority sector instructions, the draft of which was released on Thursday, a major proposal would prevent banks from excluding trade bills discounted under letters of credit from adjusted net bank credit (ANBC) when calculating PSL obligations. While such exposures can be treated as interbank credit for capital adequacy and the Large Exposure Framework, the underlying credit goes to the constituent borrower and qualifies as domestic bank credit under Form A of the RBI Act. The draft would restrict interbank treatment to capital adequacy calculations.The change could raise banks' lending obligations. Every Rs 10,000 crore of discounted bills retained in ANBC would increase the 40% PSL requirement by Rs 4,000 crore.The additional obligations would include Rs 1,800 crore for agriculture, Rs 1,400 crore for non-corporate farmers, Rs 1,000 crore for small and marginal farmers, Rs 750 crore for micro-enterprises and Rs 1,200 crore for weaker sections. The farmer sub-targets overlap with the overall agricultural target.Corporate banks could face a compliance gap because bills discounted for conglomerates, infrastructure contractors and wholesale vendors would expand the ANBC denominator without adding eligible PSL assets.Only bills involving qualifying borrowers, such as MSME suppliers, would contribute to PSL achievement. Banks may therefore need additional rural lending or PSLC purchases.The financial burden could be significant for corporate bill discounting, which typically earns spreads of 50-90 basis points. Banks may have to buy PSLCs at 80-120 basis points or place funds with development finance institutions at 200-400 basis points below the Bank Rate. They could pass on 15-30 basis points of additional compliance costs to corporate borrowers.
Article Summary: RBI proposes tighter rules for classifying gold-backed farm loans as priority sector lending (PSL) Banks would have to verify borrowers' actual agricultural credit needs against the district scale of finance for the crop. Banks would also have to document field inspections, crop hypothecation and evidence of agricultural activity by landless cultivators.

Article Title: OVL looks to operate 2 Venezuelan oil projects
Article Text:
.

NEW DELHI: ONGC's overseas investment arm ONGC Videsh (OVL) is exploring the possibility of securing operatorship rights for two Venezuelan oil projects - San Cristobal and PetroCarabobo -- and is in advanced talks with the Venezuelan govt and US authorities.During an analyst call following its Q2 financial results, the company said the arrangement is likely to be finalised in three-to-six months. The proposed agreements would give OVL greater control over field operations, production, marketing and handling of revenues. OVL, which holds a 40% participating interest in the San Cristobal project through a joint venture with PDVSA, expects to become its sole operator and sell its output, while securing joint operatorship of PetroCarabobo, in which it has an 11% stake. Under the new arrangement, the company may also acquire more stakes in more Venezuelan oilfields.ONGC finance head Anupam Agarwal said the company's pending dividends of $500 million from the two projects are likely to be adjusted after the new operatorship agreements are finalised.Driven by India's quest for energy security, OVL entered Venezuela to tap into the world's largest oil reserves but has faced major disruptions.
Article Summary: ONGC's overseas investment arm ONGC Videsh (OVL) is exploring the possibility of securing operatorship rights for two Venezuelan oil projects. The proposed agreements would give OVL greater control over field operations, production, marketing and handling of revenues. OVL expects to become its sole operator and sell its output.

Article Title: Social media platforms urged to act on digital arrest scams
Article Text:
.

NEW DELHI: Electronics and IT minister Ashwini Vaishnaw called on social media platforms to take greater responsibility for the content they carry, pressing them to explain how their algorithms work, protect children from harmful content and give users a better way to resolve complaints.Asked whether govt was considering withdrawing safe-harbour protection for social media companies, Vaishnaw left the question open. He said the internet had changed and platforms needed to act proactively on child safety, women's safety and scams such as digital arrests, in which fraudsters pose as law enforcement officers."Throughout the Parliament debates, we have maintained that social media should take responsibility for the content. They must take all the steps that are necessary for child safety," he said.Vaishnaw linked child safety to what platforms show young users. He called for greater transparency about the algorithms that recommend content and said platforms should ensure children see material appropriate for them. He said the issue had implications for both their mental and physical health.The minister also questioned the options available to users when content on a platform causes serious harm. He said users often have little recourse beyond approaching the police or going to court and called for a more effective way for them to raise grievances and get them addressed.Vaishnaw said govt had repeatedly raised these concerns with social media companies. "There has to be a good, very effective mechanism by which citizens get a voice to address their grievances."
Article Summary: Electronics and IT minister Ashwini Vaishnaw called on social media platforms to take greater responsibility for the content they carry. VaishNaw said the internet had changed and platforms needed to act proactively on child safety, women's safety and scams.

Article Title: Rupee rises 57 paise to close at 6-month high of 93.91
Article Text: MUMBAI: The rupee strengthened 57 paise to close at 93.91 a six-month high against the US dollar, extending its recovery on sustained foreign fund inflows, falling crude oil prices and easing concerns over the global concentration of investments in artificial intelligence. The currency has emerged as the second-best performer against the dollar this month after spending much of the year among the weakest emerging-market currencies.
Article Summary: The rupee strengthened 57 paise to close at 93.91 a six-month high against the US dollar. The currency has emerged as the second-best performer against the dollar this month after spending much of the year among the weakest emerging- market currencies.

Article Title: Pollution drives sales of air purifiers
Article Text:
.

NEW DELHI: Sales of air purifiers are witnessing a sharp jump as pollution levels worsen across the country, even as the onset of winter spurs demand for other seasonal appliances including room heaters, geysers and electric kettles. Air-purifier sales on Amazon doubled over the past week alone, while those across e-commerce platforms grew 1.4 times in Sept-Oct compared with the same period last year.Quick-commerce platforms, including Blinkit, Zepto and Instamart too, are seeing a sharp rise in demand, with consumers in Tier 2 cities adding to the growth momentum, analysts and industry experts told TOI.Daily sales of winter appliances on Q-commerce touched Rs 29 lakh in Oct, up 55% from Sept and 50% over Oct last year. Air purifiers led the month-on-month surge, with daily sales jumping 3.7x to Rs 9.6 lakh, while room-heater sales rose 1.6x to nearly Rs 10 lakh, data culled from 1DigitalStack, a market intelligence platform, said.The trend points to an early start to the seasonal buying cycle, with online sales expected to scale up further as temperatures dip. Typically, about 3 in 10 winter appliance sales are registered online."We are projecting a robust 31% year-on-year growth for the winter appliance category - specifically geysers, room heaters and electric kettles across e-commerce platforms. This season's surge is heavily catalyzed by the flagship annual festive sales on Amazon and Flipkart marketplaces, which have shifted consumer behaviour towards front-loading their winter utility purchases to maximise discounts,'' Samiran Mathur, VP insights and strategy at 1DigitalStack said.The current demand in these appliances is just a fraction of the expected peak. Last year, the quick commerce winter appliance market multiplied 5.7x from Oct to Nov, eventually hitting a Jan peak that was nearly 10x the Oct baseline, the data said. "With the onset of winters, we are seeing air-purifier sales on Amazon.in growing 2x in the last week. Customers are using Rufus, our personalised AI shopping assistant, to find the right fit. To serve immediate needs, we have expanded our air purifier selection on Amazon Now," an Amazon India spokesperson said.
Article Summary: Air-purifier sales on Amazon doubled over the past week alone. Air purifiers led the month-on-month surge, with daily sales jumping 3.7x to Rs 9.6 lakh. Room- heater sales rose 1.6x to nearly Rs 10 lakh.

Article Title: Bosch Q2 revenue rises 28%, net up 19%

Article Title: Crude cost for Indian companies at 2-month low
Article Text: New Delhi: The cost of oil for Indian refiners fell to $94.5 per barrel on Thursday, its lowest level in two months, amid hopes of a resolution to the US-Iran conflict and an exemption for commercial ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz. The Indian basket fell 20.4% in a week, from $118.7 on Oct 30. After hovering around $90 a barrel in the last week of Aug, the crude basket price started rising from Sept 1 and touched a peak of $130.2 before moderating, but remained around $120 a barrel through Sept and Oct, amid continued hostilities in West Asia.

Article Title: Decline in gold price pushes jewellery sales on Dhanteras
Article Text:
.

NEW DELHI: A dip in gold prices drew shoppers to jewellery stores on Dhanteras on Friday. Carmakers lined up thousands of festive deliveries, while televisions led demand at an electronics retailer.Senco Gold & Diamonds reported sales growth of more than 25% by value, with footfall up 10-12% from last year, CEO Suvankar Sen said.Kalyan Jewellers said its price for 22-carat gold fell Rs 235 a gram from Thursday to Rs 13,150 on Friday. Executive director Ramesh Kalyanaraman said footfall picked up, with shoppers favouring lighter pendants, bangles and chains, as well as smaller gold and silver coins. The chain saw more first-time buyers in cities such as Jaipur, Dehradun and Raipur."The dip in gold prices helped to boost demand, as many buyers who were waiting for a correction stepped in," said Paul Alukkas, managing director of Jos Alukkas.In Delhi's Madangir jewellery market, Ramavtar Soni, director of Prabhu Dayal & Sons Jewellers, said demand for gold and silver coins has risen, with shoppers buying them as symbols of prosperity on Dhanteras. Rama Krishna Jewellers added that the recent price dip had encouraged purchases and that shoppers continued to see gold as a store of value.Giva founder and CEO Ishendra Agarwal said 9-carat jewellery, introduced four months ago, accounted for about a quarter of revenue for its gold and lab-grown diamond business."Buying patterns are evolving, with consumers increasingly gravitating towards lightweight, versatile designs that offer value without compromising on aesthetics or aspiration," said Kirit Bhansali, chairman, Gem and Jewellery Export Promotion Council (GJEPC).Amazon India said the number of first-time jewellery shoppers rose more than 20% from the comparable festive period last year, with growth exceeding 40% in smaller cities. Flipkart Minutes said orders for gold coins and bars more than doubled in the run-up to Dhanteras. Quick commerce accounted for 80% of Bigbasket's coin orders, with one-gram gold coins the most popular.Auto companies also enjoyed strong demand. "We are expecting to deliver around 30,000 vehicles on Dhanteras this year," said Partho Banerjee, senior executive officer for marketing and sales at Maruti Suzuki India. The estimate is lower than the 41,000 deliveries Maruti reported in 2025 as Dhanteras was spread over two days. This festival season -- from Ganesh Chaturthi in Sept to Nov 6 -- the country's largest carmaker has sold 4 lakh vehicles compared with a little under 3.5 lakh last year.Hyundai Motor India's estimate covered both Dhanteras and Diwali. "We expect to deliver around 16,000 units, nearly 14% higher than last year," said MD and CEO Tarun Garg."Dhanteras saw an outstanding response, with single-day deliveries expected to cross 12,000 vehicles," said Amit Kamat, chief commercial officer at Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles.Mahindra & Mahindra said it was operating at full capacity, with physical dealer stocks close to zero across most of its SUV range. Rajesh Jejurikar, executive director and CEO of its auto and farm sector, said the company was sticking to its outlook of mid-to-high-teen SUV growth in FY27.
Article Summary: A dip in gold prices drew shoppers to jewellery stores on Dhanteras. Senco Gold & Diamonds reported sales growth of more than 25% by value. Amazon India said the number of first-time jewellery shoppers rose more than 20%.

Article Title: Antonio Brown avoids 30-year prison sentence after pleading guilty in 2025 Miami shooting case
Article Text:
Antonio Brown

Antonio Brown gets three years of probation instead of prison time

"My client was facing 30 years in prison with a 20-year minimum mandatory, and he was given an offer he just couldn't refuse,"

"get back to life"

What happened in Antonio Brown's 2025 Miami shooting case ?

A major legal chapter closes for the former NFL star

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Antonio Brown can finally put one major legal headache behind him. The former NFL superstar appeared in a Miami courtroom on Friday and pleaded guilty to a reduced charge connected to the 2025 shooting incident that once threatened to land him behind bars for decades. But the outcome was considerably different from what many might have expected when the case first made headlines. Instead of facing a lengthy prison sentence, Brown, 38, was sentenced to three years of probation after pleading guilty to aggravated assault with a firearm.The decision brings a significant development in a case that originally involved a second-degree attempted murder charge. Brown's attorney, Mark Eiglarsh, appeared pleased with the outcome, explaining that his client had been facing a potential 30-year prison sentence, including a mandatory minimum of 20 years.Eiglarsh said after the hearing.Judge Marisa Tinkler Mendez handed Brown a three-year probation sentence during Friday's proceedings in Miami state court.However, there are conditions attached to the agreement. Brown must attend weekly counseling sessions and is prohibited from possessing firearms during his probation.The plea agreement also allows him to avoid a criminal conviction through a withholding of adjudication.Brown appeared in court wearing a black leather jacket and white pants. He reportedly spoke very little during the hearing, and the judge even asked him to speak louder while entering his plea.Outside the courthouse, the former wide receiver thanked God and said he wanted toand his family.He declined to answer further questions from reporters, while his attorney described the outcome as something both sides were extremely grateful for.The legal trouble dates back to May 16, 2025, when Brown was involved in an altercation outside a celebrity boxing event in Miami. According to police and the arrest warrant, Brown allegedly grabbed a handgun from a security staffer after getting into a fistfight with Zul-Qarnain Kwame Nantambu. He was accused of firing two shots at the man, with one bullet reportedly grazing Nantambu's neck.Brown, however, maintained that he was defending himself. He claimed that he was being attacked and that people were attempting to steal his jewelry. His legal team also relied on Florida's Stand Your Ground law, arguing that Brown believed he was protecting himself from an attack.Prosecutor Howard Rosen explained during Friday's hearing that there were questions about whether Brown actually intended to shoot Nantambu, who had reportedly been walking away from the altercation when the shots were fired. The alleged victim had also previously said that he forgave Brown and did not want to cooperate with law enforcement.Brown spent 12 seasons in the NFL, becoming one of the league's most recognizable wide receivers. He enjoyed his best years with the Pittsburgh Steelers before joining the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, where he won a Super Bowl alongside Tom Brady during the 2020 season.His football career effectively ended in 2021 after he dramatically removed his jersey and equipment before walking off the field during a Buccaneers game.Now, after months of legal uncertainty, the former All-Pro has another opportunity to move forward. His three-year probation sentence means he avoids the prison time that once appeared possible, although he will still have to meet the court's conditions.
Article Summary: Antonio Brown pleaded guilty to aggravated assault with a firearm in a Miami court on Friday. The former NFL star was accused of firing two shots at Zul- Qarnain Kwame Nantambu in May 2025. Brown's attorney said his client was facing 30 years in prison with a 20-year minimum mandatory.

Article Title: IIT Delhi announces mental health reforms after student’s death; plans more counsellors and grievance ombudsperson
Article Text:
IIT Delhi to appoint more counsellors, introduce grievance ombudsperson after external inquiry report

External inquiry committee submits report

Student representatives contribute to implementation plan

Re-entry support and grievance redressal measures

External review of wellness policy planned

NEW DELHI: The Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Delhi has announced a series of institutional reforms to strengthen its mental health support system and student welfare measures following the death of student Rishikesh Kumar on August 22, 2026. The institute issued a press release, clarifying the status of an external inquiry and the steps being taken to implement its recommendations.The statement comes amid speculative reports in sections of the media concerning the circumstances surrounding the student’s death and the findings of the External Inquiry Committee. IIT Delhi said the committee’s report would remain confidential, as directed by the panel, and that its recommendations primarily address systemic changes in mental health support and related institutional mechanisms.The External Inquiry Committee was chaired by retired Delhi High Court judge Justice Mukta Gupta. Its members included a senior domain expert from the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS) and two student representatives.Following submission of the report, an internal committee examined each recommendation and prepared an operational roadmap for implementation and follow-up.The internal panel comprised the Deputy Director (Operations), Dean of Student Affairs, Dean of Academics, General Secretaries of the Student Affairs Council (SAC) and Board of Student Welfare (BSW), and the Assistant Registrar (Student Affairs).IIT Delhi stated that it shared the external committee's recommendations, proposed follow-up actions and operational roadmap with students, faculty members and staff on October 31, 2026.The proposed action plan was discussed at the SAC meeting held on November 3, 2026. According to the institute, students' inputs were incorporated directly into a time-bound implementation plan.The initiatives include extensive awareness campaigns covering mental health issues and laws concerning substance use. The institute also plans to recruit additional full-time clinical psychologists and counsellors, along with visiting psychiatrists, to expand access to professional support.IIT Delhi will introduce formal re-entry protocols for students returning after extended leaves of absence. These arrangements will include specialised counselling, academic coordination and buddy networks to support their transition back to campus.The institute also plans to establish an independent Student Grievance Ombudsperson as part of an integrated grievance redressal mechanism.A separate external committee will review the institute's Mental Health Support System and Wellness Policy. It will comprise two senior mental health experts, one welfare professional and two student representatives.The review will examine existing provisions, emergency-response protocols, referral mechanisms and monitoring arrangements before recommending changes.Mandatory empathy, soft-skills and mental health workshops will also be conducted for administrative staff, hostel personnel and faculty members.IIT Delhi said the measures form part of its efforts to strengthen student welfare and develop a more empathetic, transparent and resilient campus environment.
Article Summary: IIT Delhi to appoint more counsellors, introduce grievance ombudsperson after external inquiry report. IIT Delhi will introduce formal re-entry protocols for students returning after extended leaves of absence. Initiatives include extensive awareness campaigns covering mental health issues and laws concerning substance use.

Article Title: Diwali bank holidays: Will banks remain closed for Dhanteras, Diwali and other festivals - Check state-wise list
Article Text:
Bank holidays on Diwali

Where and where will banks remain closed:

November 9:

November 10:

November 11:

How will bank holidays affect customers

NEW DELHI: Banks across several states in India will remain closed on multiple days in November 2026 as Diwali celebrations and related regional festivals bring a series of holidays. The closures will be observed on November 9, 10 and 11, depending on the state and the festival being celebrated.Known as the festival of lights, Diwali is not limited to a single day. Celebrations extend across several days, with each occasion carrying its own cultural and regional significance. This year, bank holidays have been scheduled for Diwali, Laxmi Puja, Govardhan Puja , Bali Pratipada, Bhai Dooj and other related observances.Banks in Tripura, Madhya Pradesh, Chandigarh, Sikkim, Manipur, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh and Chhattisgarh will remain closed for Diwali/Laxmi Puja (Deepawali), Govardhan Pooja and Vishwakarma Day.Banks in Gujarat, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Uttarakhand and Sikkim will remain closed for Diwali (Bali Pratipada), Deepawali (Govardhan Puja), Laxmi Puja and Vikram Samvant New Year Day.Banks in Sikkim, Manipur, Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal and Himachal Pradesh will remain closed for Laxmi Puja (Deepawali), Ningol Chakkouba, Bhratridwitiya, Bhaidooj and Chitragupt Jayanti.Bank customers need to check the holiday schedule for their location, as closures depend on the regional festival or occasion being observed.Apart from festival-related closures, scheduled and non-scheduled banks also observe holidays on the second and fourth Saturdays of every month, in line with the Reserve Bank of India's holiday schedule.A branch closure does not mean customers lose access to all banking services. ATMs, Unified Payments Interface (UPI), internet banking and mobile banking applications remain available for routine transactions, including fund transfers, bill payments and account management.The main inconvenience is for transactions that require a visit to a physical branch. Customers planning large cash deposits, cheque processing, demand drafts or other branch-dependent work may have to wait until their branch reopens.With several holidays scheduled across November, checking the applicable state calendar before visiting a branch can help customers plan their banking requirements and avoid delays.
Article Summary: Banks across several states in India will remain closed on multiple days in November 2026. Bank holidays have been scheduled for Diwali, Laxmi Puja, Govardhan Puja, Bali Pratipada, Bhai Dooj and other related observances.

Article Title: Elon Musk's futuristic dream vehicle to cease production - What went wrong with Tesla's Cybertruck
Article Text:
Why is Elon Musk pulling the plug on Tesla's Cybertruck

1. Sales and pricing failed to meet expectations

2. Its design made it impossible to ignore

3. Musk's political image became a problem for some customers

Tesla's Cybertruck arrived with big ambitions, a futuristic design and Elon Musk 's backing.Now, it is bidding adieu.The high-tech pickup was meant to shake up the automobile industry, but its journey is coming to an end. Musk announced on Friday that Tesla would wind down Cybertruck production around the middle of 2027 at its facility outside Austin, Texas.The move will make room for increased production of the company's Cybercab robotaxi, as Tesla shifts its focus towards autonomous vehicles.But what led to the Cybertruck's early exit? A combination of disappointing sales, a price tag that was much higher than initially promised and growing controversy surrounding Musk.Musk had projected annual production of 250,000 Cybertrucks, but sales remained far below that target. Kelley Blue Book estimated that Tesla sold just 20,237 units last year, around half the previous year's sales. Sales through September this year fell another 28%. Spencer Penn, a former Tesla executive who left before the Cybertruck's launch and now heads software developer LightSource, said electric trucks had struggled to attract demand.“A really controversial vehicle unveiled by a controversial individual into a market where none of the electric trucks have been able to really capture demand,” he said.Pricing was another hurdle. Musk had promised a price tag below $40,000, but the first Cybertrucks sold for double that amount or more. Penn, who had booked a pre-sale reservation, eventually decided against buying one after the promised price failed to materialise.With its sharp angles and stainless-steel body, the Cybertruck looked more like a science-fiction vehicle than a conventional pickup. Its 2019 unveiling grabbed attention when a Tesla designer threw a metal ball at its supposedly unbreakable glass, only for the window to shatter. A second attempt on another window ended the same way. Musk, however, remained convinced about his vision.“I just wanted to make a futuristic battle tank — something that looks like it could come out of ‘Blade Runner’ or ‘Aliens’ or something like that but was also highly functional,” he told Automotive News.He called it “a better sports car than a Porsche 911” and “a better truck than an F-150.” The design drew both admiration and ridicule. Armen Hareyan, whose Torque News site covers autos, said: “Few vehicles in history have generated as much attention. The Cybertruck became a cultural symbol – loved, mocked and impossible to ignore.”Penn initially found its appearance revolting and called it “madness”, but his opinion changed the more he looked at it. He eventually saw it as an example of Tesla's adventurous spirit and willingness to take risks. “Some of these bets work and some of these bets don’t,” he said.Musk's association with several right-wing figures, particularly US President Donald Trump, alienated some Tesla customers. As his image shifted from an eccentric innovator to a polarising figure trading his billions for political influence, some previously passionate owners rushed to sell their cars. Others put stickers on their bumpers reading, “I bought this before Elon went crazy.”The backlash extended to demonstrations outside Tesla showrooms, with organisers also urging investors to sell their shares. Some protests turned violent, with Molotov cocktails thrown at Tesla vehicles, charging stations set ablaze and dealerships covered in graffiti. Cybertruck owners faced hostility too, with some being shouted at with “Nazi!” and receiving extended middle fingers.Ross Blankenship, a Cybertruck owner, said that he disliked seeing a vehicle he loved turned into a political symbol. Its futuristic appearance had reminded him of “Halo”, the science-fiction video game he played as a child.“I had that sort of child in me wanting to be part of something cool that would change the future of automotive,” Blankenship said in a call from his Cybertruck as he drove through Sunnyside, Colorado.Although he said he agreed with Musk on politics, he was unhappy about the vehicle becoming associated with the controversy.“I never bought it for any other reason than the fascination with the future technology of trucks … so that was a little heartbreaking.” The Cybertruck's discontinuation also comes as Tesla shifts its attention towards autonomous vehicles. Musk said winding down production would allow the company to make more Cybercab robotaxis, a segment on which he is betting Tesla's future.For a vehicle that Musk once called Tesla's best product, the planned shutdown marks an unceremonious end to a much-hyped project. Yet, it has not lost all its fans. Blankenship said he would buy another Cybertruck again in a heartbeat. He called the end of its production “a sad moment.”
Article Summary: Elon Musk announced on Friday that Tesla would wind down Cybertruck production around the middle of 2027 at its facility outside Austin, Texas. The move will make room for increased production of the company's Cybercab robotaxi, as Tesla shifts its focus towards autonomous vehicles.

Article Title: US stocks: Wall street bounces back in green after hitting 18-month low as chipmakers rally
Article Text:
Wall Street bounces back after days of decline

Chipmakers lead Wall Street's recovery

Texas data centre plans add to AI regulation concerns

Asian and European markets extend losses

Wall Street rebounded from its 18-month low on Friday, led by a sharp recovery in semiconductor stocks, as investors assessed the potential impact of Democratic election victories on the US artificial intelligence (AI) industry.The recovery followed a steep selloff in the previous session, triggered by fears that the election results could lead to tighter regulations for the AI sector, wiping out trillions of dollars in global stock market value. The gains were led by technology, communication services and industrial stocks.The S&P 500 rose a marginal 0.31% and the Nasdaq Composite advanced 1.1%, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average slipped 0.46%.However, despite Friday's recovery, all three indices ended the week lower following the previous session's sharp losses.Semiconductor stocks emerged as the biggest beneficiaries of Friday's rebound. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index gained 4.2%, recovering after suffering its biggest single-day decline since April 2025.Nvidia shares climbed nearly 3%, reversing some of the losses from its previous session, when the stock recorded its worst performance since January 2025.At the time, the emergence of Chinese AI model DeepSeek, which offered a low-cost alternative, had triggered a sharp market reaction.The recovery extended across other major chipmakers. AMD, Intel and Micron Technology ended the session between 5% and 11% higher. Elon Musk's Tesla and SpaceX also bounced back, gaining 4% and nearly 9%, respectively, after declining earlier in the week.Despite Friday's gains, uncertainty over the future regulatory environment continued to weigh on investor sentiment."Most of the disruption of the AI buildout will not probably occur but it's just the uncertainty of the change in government from Republican-led to Democratic-led, not only at the federal level but the state, local levels," said Gerry Sparrow, president and portfolio manager at Sparrow Capital Management."That's causing some disruption in the expectations of investors ... The volatility around elections or any political event, whether it be war or terrorist attack, is always going to disrupt the market."The prospect of tighter oversight of the AI industry is also emerging at the state level. Texas Democratic Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa said on Thursday that the state would introduce new laws to protect local communities from further large-scale data centre development.Texas already has a substantial share of data centres in the US, making the proposed measures an additional concern for investors tracking the expansion of AI infrastructure.The latest uncertainty comes as the AI trade is already facing questions over the enormous costs involved in building data centres and other infrastructure. Investors are concerned that the scale of these investments could limit future returns.These worries have added to market volatility, triggering margin calls and unsettling retail investors as well as hedge funds.Friday's recovery on Wall Street was in sharp contrast with the performance of other major global markets, where the selloff continued.European equities weakened, with the STOXX 600 declining 1%. In Asia, Japan's Nikkei and South Korea's KOSPI both plunged around 6%.The Nikkei recorded its biggest one-day decline since US President Donald Trump's "Liberation Day" trade tariff turmoil in April 2025. The fall was comparable to Wall Street's previous session, when US stocks suffered their biggest single-day decline since the same period.The broader global market indicators also remained under pressure. The MSCI All-World index fell 0.68%, while MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan dropped nearly 3%.
Article Summary: Semiconductor stocks emerged as the biggest beneficiaries of Friday's rebound. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index gained 4.2%, recovering after suffering its biggest single-day decline since April 2025. Despite Friday's recovery, all three indices ended the week lower following the previous session's sharp losses.

Article Title: US-China agree to continue trade talks as Washington presses Beijing to fulfil Busan deal commitments
Article Text:
US-China agree to keep trade talks going

China and the US have agreed to continue consultations to ensure stable and positive trade relations, local media Xinhua reported.The development comes as Washington pushes Beijing to fulfil the commitments made under the trade truce agreed between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping in Busan last year.The US has raised concerns that China is falling short of its promises on rare earth supplies, critical minerals and agricultural purchases.These concerns were discussed during a phone call on Friday morning between US treasury secretary Scott Bessent, US trade representative Jamieson Greer and Chinese vice-premier He Lifeng, who oversees trade negotiations with Washington.During the call, the US officials told China that it needed to fully deliver on the commitments made under the Busan agreement. In a post on X on Friday, he said, “ Today, US trade representative Greer and I spoke with Vice Premier He Lifeng about the US-China economic relationship and implementation of the Busan arrangement.Bessent further raised concerns about China's recent actions. "I emphasized the importance of China fully and immediately honoring its commitments, raised concerns about recent Chinese actions and underscored that progress depends on concrete results.”One of Washington's biggest concerns is China's supply of rare earths. US officials told the FT in September that China was meeting only about two-thirds of its commitments on rare earths under the Busan agreement.A person familiar with the matter said Beijing had not increased supplies even after Bessent raised the issue directly with He in New York in September, ahead of Xi's meeting with Trump in Washington.China has rejected the US claims that it is not meeting its promises on rare earth supplies.The two countries also differ over agricultural purchases. The US believes China has met its commitment to buy soyabeans but has not fulfilled its promises on other agricultural products.Washington is also concerned about China's restrictions on exports of yttrium to Japan. The rare earth is used in products ranging from jet engines to missiles. Japan makes components for products manufactured in the US, and Japanese companies have warned their government that their stockpiles of yttrium are running dangerously low.The Busan trade truce was agreed in October 2025 and was originally due to expire on January 10. However, during Xi's visit to Washington in September, the two countries extended the deadline by two months, until January 2027, after negotiators failed to resolve their differences.
Article Summary: US-China agree to keep trade talks going to ensure stable and positive trade relations. Washington pushes Beijing to fulfil commitments made under the trade truce agreed between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping in Busan last year. The US has raised concerns that China is falling short of its promises on rare earth supplies, critical minerals and agricultural purchases.

Article Title: Pakistan's external debt nearly doubles to $135 billion in 10 years, China biggest lender
Article Text:
Pakistan's external debt doubles

Pakistan's external borrowing has nearly doubled in the last 10 years, reaching $135.1 billion in 2025, with China accounting for the largest share of the country's outstanding debt among individual creditors.The increase comes as borrowing by developing economies also accelerated, taking the external debt of low- and middle-income countries to a record $9.4 trillion, according to the World Bank's International Debt Report 2026.Pakistan's external debt stood at $68.673 billion in 2015 before rising to $135.107 billion in 2025, Dawn reported, citing the World Bank report.Public and publicly guaranteed borrowing made up the bulk of the debt at $107.076 billion. This was followed by private non-guaranteed debt of $17.58 billion and short-term debt of $10.45 billion.A breakdown of the public and publicly guaranteed component shows that multilateral institutions accounted for $56.83 billion, while bilateral creditors were owed $42.43 billion. Private creditors held claims worth another $7.8 billion.Among individual lenders, China had the highest outstanding exposure to Pakistan at $22.4 billion.The World Bank followed with $19.2 billion, while the Asian Development Bank (ADB) accounted for $16.83 billion.The terms of borrowing also varied considerably depending on the source of credit. Pakistan's loans from official creditors had an average maturity of 16 years and included a four-year grace period. The average interest rate on these loans was 3.6 per cent.Private borrowing was considerably more expensive, carrying an average interest rate of 8.6 per cent. These loans had a three-year repayment period and a one-year grace period.Pakistan also received financial support from key lenders during 2025. China extended the maturities on $2 billion of its loans, while the International Monetary Fund (IMF) made $2.3 billion in fresh disbursements under the Extended Fund Facility and Resilience and Sustainability Facility arrangements. These arrangements were aimed at supporting Pakistan's long-term economic stability.The Middle East, North Africa, Afghanistan and Pakistan (Menap) region recorded improvements in its debt-service and interest ratios. However, its external debt-to-gross national income (GNI) ratio moved in the opposite direction, increasing from 26.7 per cent to 29.4 per cent in 2025.This was the biggest single-year increase in the ratio among all regions, reflecting continued accumulation of external debt.Pakistan's rising debt was part of a wider increase in external borrowing across low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). Their combined external debt grew 5.5 per cent to $9.4 trillion in 2025, marking the sharpest increase in four years.The expansion was supported by a recovery in bond issuances, a weaker US dollar and renewed interest among private investors in lending to developing economies. This also marked a forceful return of private creditors to these markets.However, access to capital markets came with higher costs, particularly for the poorest countries, which faced some of the highest borrowing costs in decades.Debt-service payments across these economies continued to climb for the fifth year in a row. At the same time, stronger economic growth helped stabilise some debt ratios, while net long-term debt transfers turned positive after several years of outflows.The increase in borrowing was more pronounced among countries eligible for International Development Association (IDA) financing. Their external debt rose 8.1 per cent to $1.3 trillion.Low-income countries recorded an even sharper increase, with external debt climbing 8.9 per cent to $262.4 billion in 2025. This was their biggest increase since 2020.
Article Summary: Pakistan's external debt stood at $68.673 billion in 2015 before rising to $135.107 billion in 2025. Public and publicly guaranteed borrowing made up the bulk of the debt at $107.076 billion. China had the highest outstanding exposure to Pakistan at $22.4 billion.
